name: Prize crossword No 24,969
preamble: Four across and four down clues have solutions that are of a kind and include no further definition.

clue.text: Disrespectful friend entertaining Queen and Prince Charles?

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside the house, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen
Prince Charles is the Queen's son; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: A friend is rude to the royals while hosting them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen and her son sit side by side inside the friend. Prince Charles was the son of Queen Elizabeth II when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal remarks are those aimed rudely at someone's looks or character, hence offensive and lacking respect.

clue.text: Henry in the end joins a Christian army that prohibits violence

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the doctrine itself, a noun

indicators.note: something placed in something else sits inside it

blocks.note: H, the henry, is the unit of inductance
an end is a goal or aim
the Salvation Army, a Christian charity organised on military lines

explanation.surface: A King Henry ends his life as a soldier in a pacifist church army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end' is not a last-letter instruction but a word meaning goal. The Salvation Army is a Christian denomination organised in military style.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahimsa is the Hindu, Buddhist and Jain principle of non-harm towards all living beings, a doctrine forbidding injury.

clue.text: Day and month for superior chaps to join in deed

indicators.note: to join in is to go inside a group, so these letters enter another piece

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October
U means upper-class, socially superior
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Gentlemen sign a legal deed on a date of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage, so it stands for superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is a legal paper, a signed written instrument, which is one kind of official record.

clue.text: Bring this if last to rise

definitions.text: Bring this if last to rise

blocks.clueFragment: Bring this if last to rise
blocks.note: surface reading: an instruction about getting someone to stand up
setter's reading: move the first two letters of the answer to its end and you get a two-word phrase meaning to rise

explanation.walkthrough: Shift the leading UP to the back and the word becomes REAR UP, which means to rise; the answer itself also means to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To uprear is an old verb for lifting or raising something upright, much like rearing up.

clue.text: Try to get number right away

indicators.note: something sent away is gone, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
a number here is something that numbs: an anaesthetic
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a figure correct straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is read as numb-er, a thing that numbs. The preamble's theme is poets, so the answer needs no definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was the great German poet of Faust, one of the themed poets the preamble describes.

clue.text: Solemn little son

blocks.note: grave means serious, solemn
S is the abbreviation for son; 'little' signals the shortening

explanation.surface: A small boy with a serious face.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words look like a definition of a sober child, but the answer is one of the preamble's poets.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Graves was an English poet and novelist, author of Goodbye to All That, so he fits the poetic theme.

clue.text: One managing to shut up the wife

indicators.note: to shut something up is to enclose it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: someone who copes is one managing
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband who manages to silence his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' reads as silencing, but here it means locking inside.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cowper was an eighteenth-century English poet, author of The Task and many hymns, one of the themed poets.

clue.text: Water channel running around home

indicators.note: running around something encircles it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a race, as in millrace, is a channel carrying water
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A stream or drain that runs round a house.
explanation.walkthrough: A millrace is the channel that feeds water to a mill wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was the French tragic dramatist who wrote in verse, Phèdre among his plays, so he counts among the poets.

clue.text: Precentor so wacky helps to make an abbey famous

definitions.text: helps to make an abbey famous

indicators.note: something wacky is crazy and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An eccentric choir leader is what makes an abbey renowned.
explanation.walkthrough: A precentor leads the singing in a cathedral or abbey, which keeps the whole surface in church. The answer also nods to the puzzle's poetic theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of Westminster Abbey where many poets are buried or commemorated is among its best-known attractions.

clue.text: Resinous substance — it is put into soothing cream

indicators.note: putting something into another thing places it inside

blocks.note: a balm is a soothing ointment
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: A sticky ingredient mixed into a calming lotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal is a standard crossword convention giving SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is an aromatic oily resin oozing from certain trees, used in medicines and perfumes.

clue.text: Luxury when university lecturer comes into old money

indicators.note: coming into a place means entering it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
U is the abbreviation for university
L is the abbreviation for lecturer
pence are money

explanation.surface: An academic lives in luxury after inheriting old family wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old money' reads as inherited wealth, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is lavish wealth and richness of living, the same idea as extravagant comfort.

clue.text: Bank offering little reward

blocks.note: first meaning: to tilt or tip over to one side, as an aircraft banks
second meaning: meagre and unprofitable, as in hard years

explanation.surface: A bank that pays poor interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a financial noun, but it is the verb for tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to tilt sideways and, as an adjective, thin or unproductive, as in lean times.

clue.text: Backed by everybody fighting the enemy?

blocks.note: first meaning: with everyone else behind you, in the leading position
second meaning: in the front line of a war

explanation.surface: A soldier in battle with the whole nation's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' sounds like support, but here it means literally having everyone behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both in the leading place, with all others behind, and serving on the battle line in war.

clue.text: Formula for action bringing dissension

blocks.note: the answer read in two parts is a recipe: change the letters of the second part
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plan of action that only causes arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read in two parts, the answer is itself an instruction whose result is the clue word, so the clue describes the answer as a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel or dispute, which is open disagreement between people.

clue.text: English business person left squashed with area inadequate for display

indicators.note: something squashed in with others is crammed among them, so it goes inside
what is inadequate falls short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
someone holding a Master of Business Administration
L is the abbreviation for left
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: An English businessman is crushed into a cramped exhibition stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squashed with area' looks like one phrase but splits: the squashing applies to the business person, and the area is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To emblazon is to show something prominently, originally to decorate a shield with heraldic devices.

clue.text: Out riding a three-wheeler round one end of street

indicators.note: one end of a word is its first or last letter; here the opening one
going round something surrounds it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: to ride is to be on a vehicle
a trike is a tricycle
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone out on a tricycle circling at the end of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like part of the cycling scene, but it is the definition: workers who are out have downed tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who are out are refusing to work in an industrial dispute, which is the same as striking.

clue.text: The sound of a small stream

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is said, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: a brook is a small stream

explanation.surface: The babbling noise of a little stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling gains a final E but the word is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke was the English war poet of The Soldier, one of the themed poets the preamble points to.

clue.text: Carpet with its first bit turned over

indicators.note: turning a letter upside down changes it into a different letter

blocks.note: Wilton is a type of woven carpet, named after the Wiltshire town
the opening W, flipped upside down, looks like M

explanation.surface: A rug with one corner flipped back.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilton is a well-known make of carpet; invert its W and it becomes an M.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton was the English poet of Paradise Lost, so he belongs with the other themed poets.

clue.text: Black as the one who was jailed in America?

definitions.text: Black as the one who was jailed in America?

blocks.clueFragment: Black as the one who was jailed in America?
blocks.note: surface reading: a dark-skinned prisoner in the US
setter's reading: Conrad Black, the newspaper proprietor and peer imprisoned in the US for fraud

explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised at the start, Black hides a surname: Lord Black owned the Daily Telegraph and served a US prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful newspaper owner is often called by this title, and Conrad Black was a famous example.

clue.text: Japanese ware showing craft, work taking a different direction

indicators.note: going the other way means running backwards

blocks.note: a ship is a craft
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Japanese pottery displaying craftsmanship that goes in a new direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests skill, but it is a vessel. OP is the abbreviation for opus, a numbered musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Shippo is Japanese cloisonné enamel work, a decorative craft product made in Japan.

clue.text: Drink offered by exhibition centre — undrinkable black liquid

blocks.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham
tar is a black liquid no one drinks

explanation.surface: An exhibition venue serves a drink that tastes like black sludge.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEC is a large exhibition venue near Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the Greek gods and now names any delicious beverage or fruit juice.

clue.text: Diamonds perhaps for a set of garments

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the four groups in a pack of cards
second meaning: matching jacket and trousers or skirt

explanation.surface: Swapping jewels for a set of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds' reads as gems, but it is a card group; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a category of playing cards and a matching outfit of clothing.

clue.text: As saint only half sweet, I grimace

indicators.note: keeping only half of something throws the rest away

blocks.note: a bonbon is a sweet
taken as written
to pull a face is to grimace

explanation.surface: A saint admits he is only half nice and pulls a face.
explanation.walkthrough: A bonbon conveniently splits into two equal halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Boniface was the eighth-century English missionary to the Germans, a canonised holy man.

clue.text: Minister is scoundrel when meeting goddess

blocks.note: a cur is a contemptible man
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A clergyman behaves like a rogue whenever he meets a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate, the Greek goddess of folly, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant parish priest, one of the clergy who serve a church congregation.

clue.text: One getting bothered about politicians

indicators.note: something bothered is ruffled and disturbed, so the letters are mixed up
to be about something is to surround it

blocks.note: taken as written
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone getting annoyed about politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs are Members of Parliament, the British name for elected politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: William Empson was an English poet and critic, author of Seven Types of Ambiguity, so he fits the poet theme.

clue.text: Messing about, no good

indicators.note: 'no' means without, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: larking about is fooling around
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Fooling around does no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' reads as a verdict, but it tells you to drop a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was the English poet of The Whitsun Weddings, another of the themed poets.
